Our Out of School program combines hands-on STEM exploration with social and emotional learning through place-based experiences in local freshwater ecosystems. Description

The WORX Project is a series of week-long, summer camp experiences happening throughout July! Each day we will travel out to the WORX Project’s property, known as Camp Woodson, which features a lake, a small hiking trail, a garden, a small lodge, and plenty of open space for activities! Students attending the WORX Project can expect to try their hands in trades like woodworking, paddle-boarding, outdoor culinary, masonry, fly fishing, and so much more! We’re working to change the way young people think about education and skilled careers, and to show our community that hands-on work is both meaningful and in demand- the journey starts here.

Description

In a time when teenagers are becoming more glued to technology, our Campers in Leadership Training (CILT) program brings participants into nature, teaches them valuable lessons about the outside world, and molds them into capable young adults.

CILTs learn from experience as they shadow counselors and develop an appreciation for hard work and the great outdoors. More than assistants, they have the opportunity to lead activities and projects and design curriculum. They attend weekly leadership trainings and set specific and achievable goals for the summer.

The CILT program is one part structured learning, one part self-guided leadership, and a big helping of fun and adventure for youth ages 12-15. There is an interview process after registration has been completed.

Program Website

Description

Our youth-serving programs are Afterschool, Summer Camp, and Advocacy & Outreach. We provide a safe, nurturing environment filled with engaging activities for Asheville City Schools and Buncombe County Schools students. YTL offers academic support and enrichment that complements and extends the learning taking place during the regular school day. We can provide transportation for scholars whose families do not have working transportation (i.e. on a very limited, as needed basis)

YTL Advocacy and Outreach is designed to serve as the “Trinity Connector” between parents, school staff, and the scholars. The program was created to bridge the gap that often widens as students enter middle school and gain more independence. The goal is to support scholars at points of transition while strengthening connections. Advocacy and Outreach coordinators collaborate with students, families, and the school system to promote the social and emotional well-being, safety, and educational success of our community’s scholars. Our Advocates connect children and families to resources, such as mental health services, college and career preparation, mentorship, mindfulness practices, and creative programming.
